title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model yet, and hands it to cyber defenders first
summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Carbon on Wednesday, calling it its strongest model, with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon skills. Google says it ranks No. 1 on version 5 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59, and leads on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities (88.2%), ExploitGym for exploitation (54.8%), and CWE-bench for patching (71.0%). It arrives just two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon. Rollout is deliberate: starting this week, a subset of cyber defenders gets access, then more trusted partners through Google’s Fairwind program, with developers, businesses, and consumers to follow once guardrails are tuned. Google is taking part in the U.S. government’s voluntary pre-release testing. Introductory pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, rising later to $4 and $20.

title: Anthropic gives every level of U.S. government a 40% discount on Claude
summary: Anthropic and the General Services Administration expanded their OneGov deal, giving government buyers a 40% discount on token-based use of Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API, with no minimum purchase. For the first time it covers state, local, tribal, and territorial governments, not just federal agencies. Anthropic estimates the discounts could save the government $1 billion and says about 500 U.S. government organizations now use Claude, with weekly Claude for Government users up about eightfold since February. The deal replaces a $1-per-user offer that expires October 31.

title: Cloudflare says an AI model on its platform sent 155 answers containing other customers’ data
summary: Cloudflare disclosed that its hosted GLM-5.3 model on Workers AI returned 155 responses containing data from other customers’ requests between August 27 and September 9. A memory pool sized smaller than the model’s context length, combined with a bug in the open-source SGLang inference engine, left stale cached data from earlier requests visible when some long prompts were rejected. Cloudflare says it found no evidence of deliberate exploitation, fixed its configuration, and patched the engine; it advises anyone running SGLang to upgrade to version 0.5.22 or later.

title: S&P 500 futures slip as Alphabet’s results revive worries about AI spending
summary: Nasdaq futures fell about 1% early Thursday as Alphabet’s results reignited concerns over soaring AI costs, Reuters reported, while investors awaited a key inflation reading a day after the Federal Reserve left rates unchanged. Yahoo Finance had S&P 500 futures down 0.2% and Dow futures just below flat, with chip stocks including Nvidia, AMD, and Micron sliding after hours. Microsoft rose after its results, offering some relief. Amazon reports after Thursday’s close, along with Intel, while Eli Lilly, Mastercard, and Caterpillar also report today.

title: Alphabet sinks about 10% premarket, on course for its worst post-earnings drop ever
summary: Alphabet shares were about 10% lower in premarket trading Thursday after its third-quarter results, CNBC reported. The Google parent posted negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion, far worse than the $2.70 billion analysts expected, and kept its full-year capital spending guidance of $195 billion to $205 billion. A close more than 9.77% lower would be its worst post-earnings reaction since it went public in 2004. Investing.com noted capital spending rose $6.5 billion from the prior quarter to $51.4 billion, ad revenue grew at its slowest pace in five quarters, and management said searches in its AI Mode are earning money more slowly than traditional searches.

title: Microsoft climbs as Azure grows 48% and spending comes in below forecasts
summary: Microsoft gained in premarket trading after cloud growth accelerated again, Investing.com reported. Azure grew 48%, overall revenue rose 19% to $92.28 billion, and adjusted profit was $4.89 a share, both above Wall Street expectations. CNBC reported capital spending and finance leases of $45.2 billion, up 30% from a year ago but below the $50.67 billion analysts projected, and free cash flow down 27% to $18.63 billion but still positive. Earlier this week Microsoft said it would offer buyouts to a large part of its workforce.

title: NVIDIA’s open Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe turns meeting audio into transcripts, translations, and answers
summary: NVIDIA introduced Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open-weight speech model that handles transcription, speaker labels, and translation in one promptable model, and can answer questions about the audio, such as listing the decisions made in a meeting. It transcribes 40 languages, including seven Indic languages. NVIDIA says it ranks No. 1 on Hugging Face’s Open ASR leaderboard with about 4.3 billion active parameters, and it’s available now on Hugging Face, with quantized versions for local machines coming soon.

title: New startup Particle launches Particle-1, a coding model that uses about 45% fewer tokens
summary: Particle launched with Particle-1, a software-engineering model post-trained on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. The company says reinforcement learning in its own training environments taught the model to solve tasks with fewer tokens while keeping accuracy, using about 45% fewer tokens on average, which cuts costs and finishes tasks sooner. Particle-1 is available now through the Particle API, with other domains planned for later releases.

title: AI agent swarms computer-check “the enormous theorem,” math’s longest proof
summary: Axiom released what it calls the first complete computer-checked proof of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups, whose original proof runs about 15,000 pages across more than 500 articles by about 100 mathematicians. Over 24 days, its engineers and mathematicians directed swarms of AI agents that wrote about 43.1 million lines in the Lean proof assistant. Along the way they found 34 noteworthy deviations from the published record and a new group theory result. The code is public, but outside experts still need to rebuild it and confirm the Lean statement says what the theorem says.

title: Rime’s Prism speech-to-speech model answers in about 300 milliseconds
summary: Rime launched Prism, which it calls the first composable speech-to-speech model for businesses. Rime says it replies to spoken audio in about 300 milliseconds, makes tool calls while it’s still talking, and keeps an inspectable text layer so companies can run guardrails before the model speaks.

title: A 17-year-old taught himself AI to build a pothole-spotting app, and Utah’s DOT is testing it
summary: Ivan Turan, a senior at West High School in Salt Lake City, built Pothole AI, an iPhone app that spots potholes in real time from a dashboard-mounted phone, logging each location with a snapshot. The idea came from road damage he saw in India and a neighbor’s story of a relative killed in a pothole crash, so he taught himself machine learning to build it. He was a 2026 National STEM Festival finalist and presented to the Utah Department of Transportation, which is now testing the app. “Use the skills that they learn, not just from school but outside of school, to create these types of solutions to big, real-world problems,” he said.

title: Inspired by his mom’s recovery, a 16-year-old built an AI tool to catch ovarian cancer early
summary: Aarnav Garg, a junior at Vernon Hills High School in Illinois, was 10 when his mother was diagnosed with Stage IV ovarian cancer; she is now cancer-free. He trained OvaScan on a public collection of ultrasound images to outline tumors and judge whether they look benign or malignant, learning machine learning through hours of tutorials. His latest prototype scored 0.916 on a standard boundary-accuracy measure, in the range of published models, and it was accepted for presentation at a medical imaging conference in Edinburgh. Clinical trials would be the next step. “Her resilience really stuck with me,” he told the Daily Herald.

title: Tonight: Dale Harris’s album release party at the Blue Moon Saloon
summary: Dale Harris celebrates a new album at the Blue Moon Saloon tonight at 7 p.m., per The Advocate’s Acadiana live music listings. Also tonight in Lafayette: D’Lovelies at Hideaway on Lee at 7 p.m., Paul Tassin at Whiskey and Vine at 6 p.m., and live music at Charley G’s Seafood Grill at 6 p.m.

title: Tonight: the UL Lafayette Symphony’s costumed Halloween Concert
summary: The UL Lafayette Symphony plays its annual Halloween Concert tonight at 7 p.m. in Angelle Hall, with musicians in costume and the audience invited to dress up. The program includes a Star Wars medley, Night on Bald Mountain, and Haydn’s Surprise Symphony, plus dancers from The Ballet Studio. Admission is $10 for adults, children free; tickets are cash or check only at the door from 6 p.m.

title: Friday: a Boo Bash for kids at the Main Library
summary: Lafayette Public Library’s Boo Bash brings music, spooky crafts, games, and treats to the Story Castle at the Main Library, 301 W. Congress St., on Friday, October 30, from 4 to 5 p.m. It’s for ages birth to 12; families are welcome and costumes are encouraged.

title: Through Saturday: the free, family-friendly Chance Haunted Ride
summary: The Chance Haunted Ride, a family-friendly Halloween ride through two decorated 18-wheeler trailers and other displays, runs nightly through October 31 from 4 to 9 p.m. at 303 Mill Valley Run. It’s free and open to the public. It started as a simple walk-through in 1995, and about 2,000 people visit each year.

title: This weekend: Blackpot Festival & Cook-off turns 20 at Vermilionville
summary: The Blackpot Festival & Cook-off celebrates its 20th year Friday, October 30, and Saturday, October 31, at Vermilionville, 300 Fisher Road. The artists page lists Jolie Holland, The Revelers, Pine Leaf Boys, Tuba Skinny, Preston Frank, and the Horace Trahan Trio, among others, and the cast-iron cook-off includes gravy, gumbo, jambalaya, Cook’s Choice, and dessert. Tasting is up to each team. Kids 12 and under get in free, and it’s rain or shine, per Lafayette Loop; check the festival’s ticket page before you go.
